articles.title: CHATGPT JUST BECAME THE NEW GOOGLE BUSINESS PROFILE, AND CMOS FINALLY GET THE NUMBERS
articles.summary: OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT, giving brands verified profiles to update company information and track mentions, profile views, and website clicks. The dashboard offers the first official data on ChatGPT visibility but doesn't reveal the prompts driving mentions. Like Google Business Profile, it could become a standard business listing with ads built in. The launch also introduces Business Agents that let shoppers ask questions and compare products inside ChatGPT.

articles.title: ABOUT A THIRD OF AMERICANS HAVE LEFT AN ONLINE COMMUNITY
articles.summary: About one-third of adults in the US have left an online community. These include groups where people connect or participate together through social media, forums, messaging, or online games. More than 80% cite losing interest as a reason, while 57% point to too much arguing and 43% to harassment. Other reasons include excessive political discussions (40%) and spending too much time online (37%). Younger adults are more likely to leave, with 44% of those under 30 having exited a community compared with 19% of adults 65 and older.

articles.title: 236 PR IDEAS FOR GTA VI'S LAUNCH
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI launches in 9 days, which is an opportunity for non-gaming companies to earn press coverage. This post includes 236 PR ideas, grouped into 11 plays, with what each one looks like for GTA 6. Each idea is based on a real campaign that got a brand outside gaming into the press.

articles.title: GO FOR A 70-20-10 SPLIT ON LINKEDIN
articles.summary: Grow your LinkedIn following with a 70-20-10 content split across roughly 20 monthly posts. Spend 70% (14 posts) on top-of-funnel content like industry news, humor, and relatable topics to reach a broader audience. Use 20% (4 posts) for tactical playbooks that solve specific audience problems. Reserve 10% (2 posts) for social proof, client wins, and promotional offers. Maximize reach and follower growth over lead generation, with optional weekend posts or experimental content to build familiarity.

articles.title: POSTSNAG
articles.summary: PostSnag is a Chrome extension and content research tool designed to automatically capture, organize, and analyze viral Facebook posts. It saves posts, Reels, and content from any Facebook profile, business page, or group as you scroll normally. It then sorts and ranks collected posts by likes, comments, shares, video plays, and post times. It's free to install and offers paid plans with additional features.

articles.title: CHATGPT IS NOW SHOWING ADS WHILE IMAGES ARE BEING GENERATED
articles.summary: For free ChatGPT users, image generation now comes with ads attached. Labeled, multi-image units run while a picture renders for US users on the Free and Go plans. They fill the seconds a user already spends waiting for the picture, so the ad interrupts nothing. Free users can opt out of ads, but only by giving up image generation.

articles.title: BEFORE YOU SPEND MORE ON ADS, FIND OUT WHAT HAPPENED TO YOUR LAST 300 LEADS
articles.summary: Reviewing recent leads shows where the process breaks before more money goes into ads. If cost per lead is rising, the campaigns themselves likely need work. If many leads were never contacted, the problem is sales capacity, and more ads would only lengthen the queue. If leads were contacted quickly but rarely qualified, the problem is likely the offer, targeting, or form questions.

articles.title: HOW SOFTWARE BUYERS USE AI
articles.summary: AI is introducing new software vendors to buyers who already have a shortlist. Wynter's survey found that 63% of buyers with existing vendor candidates added another option through AI. Buyers then use follow-up prompts to compare vendors and evaluate pricing, integrations, setup, and product fit. After using AI, 73% visited vendor websites and 48% used Google to continue their research. Marketers need to build brand awareness before buyers start searching and make sure their products appear in AI recommendations across multiple platforms.

articles.title: WE JUST GOT RID OF TITLES AT BEEHIIV
articles.summary: beehiiv eliminated job titles to reduce internal bureaucracy and keep employees focused on customers rather than hierarchy. Managing titles created unnecessary work around leveling, promotions, and pay negotiations. These discussions led to meetings and internal politics without improving the product. Instead, employees are now identified by their job family, with “Lead” added for people managers. The company argues that growth should be measured through greater responsibilities and contributions rather than titles or rank.
